newsitem.title: USA: It's too soon to comment on tobacco deal - Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: It's too soon to comment on tobacco deal - Gingrich.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Sunday it was too early to comment on a landmark settlement between U.S. states and the tobacco industry, which has to be agreed by Congress before the deal can take effect.
"I don't have any opinion," Gingrich told reporters after a speech to about 2,000 members of the National Sheriffs Association in his home district in suburban Atlanta.
"Until we have time to have the experts look at it and review it and have hearings on it, I don't think anybody should jump to conclusions," he added.
Gingrich on Friday said the U.S. Constitution did not have any rules on whether private groups could forward bills through Congress for passage.

He made the statement after a group of state attorneys general and the tobacco industry reached a deal under which tobacco companies agreed to pay $368.5 billion, admit that tobacco is addictive and accept extensive federal regulation over their products and advertising in return for immunity from further punitive liability for any past deception, fraud or conspiracy.
Gingrich insisted his comments Friday were not meant to suggest he had a negative view of the deal.
"It's just saying that no secret group can go off and hide and come up with their deal and then tell the Congress 'pass this or nothing,'" he said.
